What is the difference between textContent, innerText, and innerHTML?
questions.answer:
textContent returns all text including hidden nodes and preserves whitespace. innerText reflects only rendered visible text. innerHTML returns the raw markup including tags.

code:
const el = document.querySelector('#box');
console.log(el.textContent);  // plain text
console.log(el.innerHTML);    // includes HTML tags

real example:
Scraped assertion text should use textContent and trim rather than innerHTML, which returns markup that breaks string comparisons.

What is event bubbling and how do you stop it?
questions.answer:
Bubbling propagates an event from the target up through its ancestors. Stopping it prevents parent handlers from running using stopPropagation.

code:
child.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.stopPropagation());

real example:
A modal close button that should not trigger the row click underneath needs stopPropagation on its handler.

What is the difference between a cookie and localStorage data?
questions.answer:
localStorage stores larger string data per origin that persists and is sent to no server, while cookies are small name-value pairs automatically sent with requests.

code:
localStorage.setItem('token', 'abc');
const t = localStorage.getItem('token');
document.cookie = 'session=xyz; path=/';  // web server cookies

real example:
UI auth filters grant access client-side via localStorage, but the same token is not available to API requests unless sent as a header.
